target_description: The instrument's reference value (valeur_reference) observed at its NEXT calibration/verification campaign, i.e. next-year drift prediction for the same instrument.
prediction_unit: UNKNOWN / REQUIRES CONFIRMATION - not recorded in the source ILA data. 'valeur_reference' is instrument-category dependent (see reports/data_dictionary/Data_Dictionary.xlsx). Do not display a fabricated unit; label the value with the target variable name only until a metrologist confirms the unit per instrument category.

feature_notes.EMT_basse: Lower bound of the Maximum Permissible Error (EMT) tolerance interval.
feature_notes.EMT_haute: Upper bound of the Maximum Permissible Error (EMT) tolerance interval.
feature_notes.max: Upper bound of the measurement interval (typically valeur_reference + incertitude).
feature_notes.min: Lower bound of the measurement interval (typically valeur_reference - incertitude).
feature_notes.consigne: Nominal/setpoint value the instrument is expected to indicate. Frequently missing in source data (~34%); median-imputed by the saved pipeline if absent.
feature_notes.valeur_reference: Reference (traceable) value recorded during the CURRENT calibration/verification.
feature_notes.rolling_min_3: HISTORICAL FEATURE - rolling minimum of valeur_reference over the instrument's last 3 campaigns.
feature_notes.rolling_max_3: HISTORICAL FEATURE - rolling maximum of valeur_reference over the instrument's last 3 campaigns.
feature_notes.rolling_mean_3: HISTORICAL FEATURE - rolling mean of valeur_reference over the instrument's last 3 campaigns.
feature_notes.rolling_median_3: HISTORICAL FEATURE - rolling median of valeur_reference over the instrument's last 3 campaigns.
feature_notes.moving_average_5: HISTORICAL FEATURE - moving average of valeur_reference over the instrument's last 5 campaigns.
feature_notes.ewm_mean: HISTORICAL FEATURE - exponentially weighted mean of valeur_reference over the instrument's history.

historical_features_warning: 6 of the 12 input features (rolling_min_3, rolling_max_3, rolling_mean_3, rolling_median_3, moving_average_5, ewm_mean) are computed from an instrument's PAST measurement history, not observable at the moment of a single new reading. The API exposes GET /model/instruments/{instrument_id}/last-known-features to pre-fill these from the training dataset's most recent known row for that instrument; the metrologist must review/confirm them before submitting a prediction.
preprocessing_description: The saved artifact is a single scikit-learn Pipeline containing SimpleImputer(strategy='median') followed by StandardScaler and the Lasso estimator, fit together on the training data. Inference MUST call pipeline.predict(dataframe) directly, with columns in feature_order, and must NOT recreate imputation or scaling manually.
cv_strategy_reference: GroupKFold (grouped by id_instrument, 5 folds) - chosen because it never splits the same instrument across train and test, unlike a naive KFold which leaks instrument identity.
known_limitations: IMPORTANT: On this dataset (741 rows, 22 instruments), a trivial persistence baseline (predict next value = current valeur_reference) achieves a LOWER MAE (1.95) and higher EMT-conformity agreement (92.5%) than this trained Lasso model (MAE 4.98, conformity agreement 47.5%) under GroupKFold cross-validation. This is a documented, reproducible finding from notebooks/05_Regression_Model.ipynb (section 11), not a bug in this API.

This Lasso model is served because it is the best-performing LEARNED model, saved for explainability/tuning purposes by the training notebook. It has NOT been shown to outperform the trivial 'no drift' baseline at the current data volume.

No scientifically validated drift threshold exists in this project. The API and UI must never label a prediction 'safe', 'critical', or 'dangerous' - only 'prediction generated', with a neutral, factual interpretation.
This tool is a decision-support aid. It must never automatically replace a metrologist's professional judgement, and does not by itself constitute ISO/IEC 17025 evidence of conformity.

DATA QUALITY (raw Excel source, not a pipeline bug): openpyxl formula inspection of data/raw/*.xlsx found an off-by-one row-drag error in the min/max formulas of sheets 'lab 47a', 'lab 47b' (and their 2025 variants) across ILA60-22, ILA60-24, ILA61-23, ILA61-2025: the formula for measurement points 3 through 10 references the NEXT row's uncertainty cell instead of its own. Point 10 (last row) references a blank cell, producing min=max=valeur_reference exactly (visibly wrong). Points 3-9 silently use the WRONG uncertainty value (plausible-looking, not visibly wrong) for min/max/conforme. 176 affected cells precisely listed in reports/quality/DONNEES_A_VALIDER_decalage_formule_47a_47b.csv for metrology-expert review. No measurement was altered by this audit -- per project policy, this requires human/metrology validation, not an automated fix.

BUG FIXED (2026 audit): model_service.py previously trusted metadata.json feature_order for column ordering at prediction time, which had drifted out of sync with the actually fitted pipeline order -- causing /predict to fail (500 error) for essentially every request, including fully valid payloads (verified via the test suite: 2/11 tests failing before the fix). Fixed by reading the order from the pipeline's own fitted imputer.feature_names_in_ (ground truth) instead of the separately-maintained metadata file. metadata.json feature_order was also resynced for documentation accuracy. Verified: 11/11 tests pass after the fix.
